words.gloss: sahacara/sahācara (probably Barleria prionitis, prickly yellow barleria; probable)

hindi: उसी प्रकार सहाचर यानी सम्भवतः कटसरैया, बला यानी बरियार, सारिवा यानी अनन्तमूल और दर्भ यानी सम्भवतः कुश के साथ तैयार किया हुआ।
english: Likewise, prepared with sahācara (probably prickly yellow barleria), balā (country mallow), sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla) and darbha (probably sacred kuśa grass).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sāhacara' for 'sahacara/sahācara'; the vowel length varies in the print

notes: Elliptical: the noun being prepared is not stated here; it presumably continues from the preceding unit, which lies outside this chunk; no noun is supplied in the translation. Printed 'sāhacara' is read as sahacara/sahācara (the word is sahācara in unit 70). Identification of sahacara is probable only (Barleria prionitis; some sources take sahacara as kuraṇṭaka, the yellow variety); darbha as Desmostachya bipinnata is probable. Compound sandhi 'bhasādhitam' read as '-darbha-sādhitam'.

words.gloss: the pair of bṛhatī (Solanum species; the usual pair is bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī; probable)

hindi: दूध की बस्ति, उसी प्रकार अभीरु यानी सम्भवतः शतावरी, गुडूची यानी गिलोय और बृहती-द्वय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी और छोटी कटेरी के साथ।
english: A milk enema (kṣīra-basti), likewise with abhīru (probably shatavari), guḍūcī (giloy) and the pair of bṛhatī.
notes: Continues into unit 42 (milk cooked ...). 'abhīru' is a name of śatāvarī in the standard lists (probable; it is also a name of other plants). 'bṛhatī-dvaya' is read as bṛhatī with its pair kaṇṭakārī (probable); the text does not name the second plant. Plural instrumental of the pair is as printed. Avagraha printed with a stray space before it ('tathā 'bhīru...'): src kept as printed.

words.gloss: māgadhikā (Piper longum, long pepper, pippalī; standard)

hindi: दूध सिद्ध किया हुआ, मागधिका यानी पीपर और यष्टीमधु यानी मुलेठी के कल्क से युक्त।
english: Milk cooked with a paste (kalka) of māgadhikā (long pepper) and yaṣṭīmadhuka (licorice).
notes: Continues 41. 'kalkavat' read as 'having the paste (kalka) of ...'; the other reading 'like a paste' is possible. The text does not say what the milk is cooked with beyond what unit 41 gives; 41-42 may be read as one sentence (not claimed as a verse pairing).

words.gloss: pañcamūla, the group of five roots
measured by a pala (a unit of weight)
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. ud-√mā, n. nom. sg.

hindi: पञ्चमूल यानी पाँच मूल, बृहती से आरम्भ होने वाले, प्रत्येक द्रव्य एक पल तौल में मापा हुआ।
english: The pañcamūla (five roots), those beginning with bṛhatī, each drug measured at one pala.
notes: Elliptical list (no verb). 'bṛhatyādi-pañcamūla' is the group of five roots headed by bṛhatī (usually the lesser pañcamūla; probable, the text does not list them). 'pratidravyam' read as 'for each substance' with palonmitam 'measured by a pala'; the exact grammatical link is not certain. Identification (probable, from the standard lists, not from this text): the five roots headed by bṛhatī are the lesser pañcamūla - bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, gokṣura.

hindi: दो पल शालि यानी अगहनी चावल, गोधूम यानी गेहूँ, यव और माष यानी उड़द, यष्टिका यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी सहित।
english: Two palas of śāli (winter rice), godhūma (wheat), yava (barley) and māṣa (black gram), together with yaṣṭikā (probably licorice).
notes: Whether 'two palas' applies to each grain or to the whole is not decided by the text. Elliptical (no verb). Printed 'dvipalaṃ śāli' read as dvi-palam, śāli; the case of the list is taken as accusative/nominative of enumeration.

hindi: उनके साथ सिद्ध किया हुआ बकरी का दूध, कुक्कुट के अण्डे का रस और सिता यानी मिश्री।
english: Goat's milk cooked with those, the fluid (rasa) of a fowl's (kukkuṭa) egg, and sitā (crystallised sugar).

text_flags.why: possible: single k for kukkuṭa (spelling variant or scan slip); meaning unchanged

notes: 'kukuṭa' is printed for the usual kukkuṭa (spelling variant, restored in the split). 'kukkuṭa' means cock or hen; the text does not say which, 'hen' is the usual reading of egg-fluid (not firm). 'taiḥ' refers to the grains and drugs of 43-44. Elliptical list, no verb.
lines_deva: तैः सिद्धं छागलं क्षीरं कुकुटांडरसः सिता
lines_iast: taiḥ siddhaṃ chāgalaṃ kṣīraṃ kukuṭāṃḍarasaḥ sitā

words.gloss: with ghee (ājya), honey (kṣaudra) and two salts (dvi-lavaṇa)

hindi: घी, शहद और दो लवणों के साथ, उनसे बस्ति अत्यन्त शुक्र को उत्पन्न करने वाली है।
english: With ghee, honey and the two salts (dvilavaṇa), by those the enema (basti) is a maker of semen (śukra), supremely.
notes: 'dvilavaṇa' = 'two salts'; the text does not name them here, so they are left unidentified. 'param' read as adverb 'greatly/supremely'; it can also mean 'best' (adjective of bastiḥ). Verb 'is' implied. 'taiḥ' refers back to the ingredients of 44-45.

words.gloss: peacock (śikhin); first part of 'gonarda' as printed split
words.gram: dvandva member (first part of the printed split of gonarda)

words.gloss: second part of 'gonarda' (a creature whose eggs are meant; possibly a bird; unidentified)
in the fluids of the eggs of fish and the like

hindi: यह कल्प मोर, गोनर्द, मछली आदि के अण्डों के रसों में भी है।
english: This is the formula (kalpa) also in the fluids of the eggs of the peacock (śikhin), gonarda, fish and the like.

text_flags.why: possible: the space inside the compound looks like a scan/typing break

notes: 'śikhigo narda' is printed with a space; read as one name 'śikhi-gonarda' (peacock, gonarda). 'gonarda' is the name of a bird (identity uncertain: unidentified; sometimes a kind of crane). It could instead be read as a single compound 'peacock-gonarda' - not firm. 'ādi' = 'and the like' is in the text (matsyādi).

words.gloss: of the flesh of a crab (kulīra)
joined with the fluid of sparrow's eggs

hindi: केकड़े के मांस का रस, चटक यानी गौरैया के अण्डे के रस से युक्त।
english: The juice (rasa) of crab (kulīra) flesh, joined with the fluid of the eggs of the caṭaka (sparrow).
notes: 'kulīra' = crab (standard), 'caṭaka' = sparrow (standard). Elliptical, no verb. Singular 'aṇḍa' in the compound can mean one egg or eggs in general.

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, m. nom. sg. (printed madhu r- = madhuḥ before bastiḥ)

hindi: शर्करा, घी और शहद के साथ बस्ति वृषतम यानी सबसे अधिक वृष्य मानी गई है।
english: With sugar (śarkarā), ghee and honey, the enema (basti) is considered the most aphrodisiac (vṛṣatama, 'most bull-like').
notes: The printed spacing 'madhu rbastir' is a break in the middle of 'madhuḥ bastir' (visarga + b- gives r); src kept as printed. 'śarkarā' = sugar/coarse sugar (standard).

words.gloss: with the flesh of crab (kulīra) and sparrow (caṭaka)

hindi: बकरे और सूअर से उत्पन्न अण्डकोशों यानी मुष्कों से तथा केकड़े और चटक यानी गौरैया के मांस से।
english: With testes (muṣka) from the he-goat and the boar, and with the flesh of crab (kulīra) and sparrow (caṭaka).
notes: Printed 'bastamūkarajair' is read basta-mūkara-jaiḥ ('from he-goat and boar'); 'muṣka' = testis (standard, lit. 'testicles'). 'mūkara' is not a standard word; read as a slip for sūkara 'boar' (m/s confusion in the scan), possible, not firm. Elliptical (no verb); the instrumental list may continue in the next unit (not claimed as fact).

hindi: दूध सिद्ध किया हुआ बकरे के मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश, उच्चटा और इक्षुरक यानी सम्भवतः तालमखाना के साथ, तथा शहद।
english: Milk cooked with the testis of a he-goat, uccaṭā (a plant, not identified) and ikṣuraka (probably kokilākṣa, Hygrophila spinosa), and honey.
notes: The case of 'bastamuṣkam' and 'ikṣurakam' (instrumental 'with', accusative list) is not given by the print; read as ingredients of the cooked milk. 'ikṣuraka' = ikṣura, usually kokilākṣa (Hygrophila spinosa = Asteracantha longifolia) (probable). 'uccaṭā' is unidentified here (sources differ). Elliptical, no verb.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, घी से भरपूर और अल्प नमक वाली बस्ति वृषतम यानी अत्यन्त वृष्य और उत्तम है।
english: On a conjectural reading, an enema (basti) rich in ghee and with little salt is the most aphrodisiac (vṛṣatama), supreme.

text_flags.why: possible: 'nir-' makes 'rich in non-ghee'; the sense and parallel with unit 49 suggest 'rich in ghee'

notes: 'nirghṛtāḍhya' as printed would mean 'rich in what is without ghee', which is contradictory; the sense and the parallel with 49 ('ghṛta') suggest 'ghṛtāḍhya' (rich in ghee) with a stray 'nir'. The reading is a conjecture (possible); if 'nir-' were meant, the sense might be 'with the ghee drawn off' - not firm.

hindi: सिद्ध किए हुए दूध से भोज्य, आत्मगुप्ता यानी केवाँच, उच्चटा और इक्षुर यानी सम्भवतः तालमखाना के साथ।
english: Food (bhojya) with milk cooked with ātmaguptā (cowhage), uccaṭā and ikṣura.
notes: Read as 'food (bhojya) [taken] with milk cooked with ātmaguptā, uccaṭā and ikṣura'; the print does not state the verb. 'siddhena payasā' instrumental 'with cooked milk'.

hindi: इसके पश्चात् जो दस-दस दिन के क्रम से बस्तियों का सेवन करता है।
english: Thereafter, he who uses the enemas (basti) at ten-ten days.
notes: 'daśadaśāhena' is literally 'by ten-ten days'; whether it means ten days per course, or a course every ten days, is not decided by the Sanskrit. The sentence continues in 55 (the result).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, घोड़े की तरह पुष्ट हुआ, एक अस्पष्ट शब्द 'सदृषः', वह सौ स्त्रियों के पास जाता है।
english: On a conjectural reading, nourished like a stallion, [unclear word: 'sadṛṣaḥ'], he goes to a hundred women.

text_flags.why: possible: not a recognisable word; several nearby readings fit the metre

notes: 'sadṛṣo' is not a word; possibilities include 'sadṛśaḥ' (similar), 'sa-dṛḍhaḥ' (firm) or 'sa-hṛṣṭaḥ' (delighted) - none is certain, so the word is left unsplit and unglossed and no firm reading is built. The subject 'he' is the man of 54. 'gacchati' is literally 'goes to'.

hindi: ये, माक्षिक यानी शहद से संयुक्त, मनुष्य को अतिवृष यानी अत्यन्त पौरुषयुक्त बना देते हैं।
english: These, joined with honey (mākṣika), make a man exceedingly potent (ativṛṣa, 'very bull-like').
notes: 'mākṣika' = bee-honey (standard in this context; the same word also names a mineral, pyrite, in other places - not meant here, probable). 'ete' refers to the preparations just described.

hindi: और वे स्तम्भी यानी रोकने वाले, न अतियोग करते हैं और न अयोग।
english: And they, stambhin (checking, retaining), bring about neither excess (atiyoga) nor lack (ayoga).
notes: The sense of 'stambhin' ('checking, stiffening, retaining') and the agent 'they' are not firm; the sentence may speak of the preparations of 56. 'nātiyogam na cāyogam' read as 'neither atiyoga nor ayoga'. Some readings take 'stambhinaḥ te ca' differently - not decided.
lines_deva: नातियोगं न चायोगं स्तंभिनस्ते च कुर्वते
lines_iast: nātiyogaṃ na cāyogaṃ staṃbhinaste ca kurvate

hindi: प्रायः निरूह बस्तियाँ लेखन यानी खुरचने वाली और स्नेहबस्तियाँ बृंहण यानी पोषण करने वाली हैं।
english: For the most part, nirūha enemas are scraping (lekhana) and sneha enemas (sneha-basti) are nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa).
notes: 'prāyaḥ' (mostly) is placed so that it may qualify either half; taken here with the second. 'nirūha' is kept as a technical name of a kind of enema.

hindi: यापन बस्तियों में दोनों हैं, इसलिए उनमें अनुवासन इष्ट नहीं है।
english: In the yāpana enemas there is both; therefore anuvāsana (oil enema) in them is not desired.
notes: 'ubhayam' (both) is not defined by the line; it presumably refers to the two kinds of effect or enema of 58 (lekhana and bṛṃhaṇa), but the text does not say. 'yāpana' is kept as the technical name of a kind of enema. Verb 'is' implied.

words.gram: ppp. caus. pra-√yuj, m. nom. pl.

hindi: परन्तु जिसमें प्रयुक्त किए गए ये मृदु होने के कारण वापस न लौटें।
english: But he in whom these, when administered, should not return because of mildness.
notes: Doubled 'rtt' in 'nivartteran' is normalised to 'rt' in the split. 'nivartteran' is literally 'should turn back'; the sense is presumably 'are not expelled', but the text only says 'return'. The sentence continues in 61.

hindi: मूत्र सहित तीक्ष्ण बस्तियों से आस्थापन करके वह शीघ्र ही।
english: Having given an āsthāpana (nirūha) with sharp enemas together with urine, he quickly indeed.
notes: GROUPING: units 60-61 read as one sentence (60 "but he in whom these ... should not return", continued in 61), but the verb is missing in 61; either the main clause is lost or 'saḥ' begins a clause that continues in the next unit. The subject of 'āsthāpya' (physician) and the 'he' (saḥ) are not both clear. No verb is supplied.

hindi: सूजन, अग्नि का नाश, पाण्डुता यानी फीकापन, शूल, अर्श यानी बवासीर और परिकर्तिका यानी काटने की पीड़ा।
english: Swelling (śopha), loss of the digestive fire (agni), pallor, colic pain (śūla), haemorrhoids (arśas, piles), and cutting pains (parikartikā).

text_flags.suggest: …śūla-arśa-parikartikāḥ (or arśaḥ read as a separate word)
text_flags.why: possible: visarga before p- inside a compound is irregular; meaning unchanged

notes: 'śopha' = swelling, oedema (standard). 'arśaḥ' is a visarga form before 'p' inside the printed compound, read as the separate word 'arśas'. Doubled 'rtt' in 'parikarttikā' normalised. The list is the subject of 'syuḥ' in 63. GROUPING: 62-63 form one sentence.

hindi: यापन के अत्यधिक सेवन से ज्वर और अतिसार यानी दस्त भी हो सकते हैं।
english: Fever and diarrhoea may occur, from excessive use of yāpana.
notes: Completes 62. 'syuḥ' is plural and covers the whole list of 62 plus fever and diarrhoea. 'atisāra' = diarrhoea (standard).

hindi: उस स्थिति में अरिष्ट, क्षार, सीधु यानी गन्ने के रस की मदिरा आदि से दीपन क्रिया यानी अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने वाला उपचार इष्ट है।
english: In that case a kindling treatment (dīpanī kriyā) with ariṣṭa, kṣāra, sīdhu and so forth is desired.
notes: 'tatra' refers to the troubles of 62-63. 'dīpana' = kindling the digestive fire (agni). 'ariṣṭa' and 'sīdhu' are kept as drink names; no further identification is made.

hindi: इसलिए युक्ति से तथा प्रसंग के अनुसार यापन का भी सेवन करे।
english: Therefore one should use yāpana too, with judgement and as occasion arises.
notes: 'yāpanāṃca' is printed without a space for 'yāpanāṃ ca'. 'prasaṅgataḥ' is rendered 'as occasion arises'; 'by repeated association/continuation' is possible. Confidence medium: the sense of 'prasaṅga' varies.

words.gloss: from the combination with mild and little drug
from a quantity reduced by a quarter

hindi: मृदु और अल्प औषध के संयोग से तथा एक चौथाई कम मात्रा से।
english: From the combination with mild and little medicine, and from a quantity reduced by a quarter.
notes: Elliptical list of reasons; the sentence is completed in 67. 'pāda' = one quarter (standard). Reading 'mild and little' vs 'mild little' of 'mṛdvalpa' is not decided.

words.gloss: from use for a short time
freedom from avoidance, absence of restriction

hindi: और थोड़े समय तक प्रयोग से भी उनमें परिहार का अभाव रहता है।
english: And from use for a short time; in those there is absence of avoidance (niṣparihāratā, no restrictions).
notes: 'parihāra' is avoidance or restraint (of food, regimen); the text does not list the restrictions. 'teṣu' refers to the yāpana enemas. Verb 'is' implied.

hindi: यापन के प्रयोजन वाले द्रव्यों में, सिद्ध स्नेह से, अलग-अलग।
english: In the drugs meant for yāpana, from cooked sneha, separately, each.

text_flags.why: possible: long ā in 'siddhā-' looks like a typing slip; the word is read as siddha-sneha

notes: 'siddhāsnehāt' is read as 'siddha-snehāt'; the long 'ā' looks like a typo (possible). Sentence completed in 69. The syntax of the ablative is not certain, hence confidence low. Possible syntax (not decided): 'pṛthak' governs the ablative, 'apart from the cooked sneha'; the repeated 'pṛthak pṛthak' then means 'each separately'.

hindi: या सभी में परिहार से रहित बस्तियों को लगाए।
english: Or in all, one should apply enemas (basti) free from restrictions.
notes: Completes 68: apply the enemas separately in the drugs or in all of them. 'sarveṣu' (in all) is read as 'in all the drugs'. The printed 'bastīnsarveṣu' is a fused pair.

words.gloss: rāsnā (disputed: Pluchea lanceolata or Alpinia galanga)
from gokṣuraka (Tribulus terrestris, puncture vine; standard)

hindi: सहाचर यानी सम्भवतः कटसरैया, अभीरु यानी सम्भवतः शतावरी, बला यानी बरियार, रास्ना जिसकी पहचान विवादित है यानी रासना या कुलंजन, और गोक्षुरक यानी गोखरू से अलग-अलग।
english: From sahācara, abhīru, balā, rāsnā and gokṣuraka (puncture vine), separately.
notes: The ablative on the last member is read as covering the whole list. rāsnā is disputed (Pluchea lanceolata is the usual choice, some sources give Alpinia galanga). The sentence continues in 71 (a tulā of each, in water). Elliptical: no verb.

words.gloss: in a hundred droṇas of water

hindi: एक तुला, सौ द्रोण जल में, पाँच द्रोण शेष रहने पर।
english: A tulā (of each), in a hundred droṇas of water, when five droṇas remain.
notes: 'tulā' and 'droṇa' are units of weight and volume and are kept in Sanskrit. The verb (boil down) is not stated. 'a tulā of each' follows 'pṛthak' in 70.

words.gloss: drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard)

hindi: छानकर ठण्डा होने पर: बिस यानी कमलनाल, द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर या मुनक्का, नत यानी सम्भवतः तगर, वक्षीरी जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है, और निदिग्धिका यानी कटेरी।
english: When strained and cooled: bisa (lotus stalk), drākṣā (grape or raisin), nata (probably tagara), vakṣīrī (unclear) and nidigdhikā (yellow-berried nightshade).

text_flags.why: possible: 'vakṣīrī' is not a recognisable plant name

notes: 'vakṣīrī' is not a recognisable plant name; it may be 'vaṃśakṣīrī' or a split such as 'va kṣīrī' - unresolved; do not rely on it. 'nata' is disputed (tagara is one reading). The drugs of 72-76 are put into the decoction in 77. Unit 72 and 73 are one list.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, औषधों की एक सूची, जिसका अधिकांश अस्पष्ट है और जिसमें महासहा नाम सम्भव है।
english: On a conjectural reading, a list of drugs, most of it unclear, in which the name mahāsahā is possible.

text_flags.why: possible: 'haṣṭī' for 'yaṣṭī'; the rest of the compound cannot be restored

notes: The printed compound is garbled ('mahāsahāṃśudrasahāyahaṣṭīmadhumūlikāḥ'); it probably contains mahāsahā, aṃśumatī (or aṃśu), a form of 'sahā', yaṣṭī (misprinted as 'haṣṭī') and madhumūlikā or madhuka, but the division is not safe. It is left unsplit and no identification is built on it. Continues the list of 72. Possible (not firm, not built into the translation): 'aṃśudrasahā' may be a corruption of 'kṣudrasahā', giving the usual pair mahāsahā + kṣudrasahā (often taken as māṣaparṇī and mudgaparṇī).

words.gloss: jīvaka (one of the aṣṭavarga drugs, identification disputed)
ṛṣabhaka (one of the aṣṭavarga drugs, identification disputed)

hindi: जीवक, ऋषभक, उदीच्य यानी सम्भवतः ह्रीवेर अर्थात् सुगन्धबाला, मृणाल यानी कमलनाल, उत्पल यानी नीलकमल और चन्दन।
english: Jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, udīcya (probably hrīvera), mṛṇāla (lotus fibre), utpala (blue lotus or water lily) and candana (sandalwood).
notes: Continues the list. jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka (usually Malaxis species of the aṣṭavarga group) have disputed identity and no identification is built here. 'udīcya' as hrīvera (Pavonia odorata) is probable.

hindi: खजूर, ताल की मज्जा यानी ताड़ की गिरी, आत्मगुप्ता यानी केवाँच, आमलकी यानी आँवला और कणा यानी सम्भवतः पीपर।
english: Kharjūra (date), the kernel (majjā) of tāla (palmyra), ātmaguptā (cowhage), āmalakī (Indian gooseberry) and kaṇā (probably long pepper).
notes: The printed 'ātmaguptānāmalakī' has an extra 'n': read as ātmaguptā + āmalakī (possible typo). 'kaṇā' commonly names long pepper (pippalī) (probable). tāla = palmyra palm (standard).

words.gloss: bark and leaf (the cinnamon pair; probable)

hindi: पटोल यानी परवल, मेदा नामक द्रव्य जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, त्वक् और पत्र, शीतपाकी, और ओदन नाम वाले।
english: Paṭola (pointed gourd), medā, bark (tvak) and leaf (patra), śītapākī, and those named odana.
notes: 'āvhayāḥ' is printed for the usual 'āhvayāḥ' ('named', possible typo). 'tvakpatra' is read as 'tvak and patra'; the cinnamon pair (bark and leaf) is a common reading but the text does not name the plant (probable). medā is disputed; śītapākī and 'odana' are unidentified.

hindi: कल्क बनाकर उसमें डाले, और अलग से एक प्रस्थ मापा हुआ।
english: Having made them into a paste (kalka), one should put (them) into that, and separately a prastha measured.
notes: 'tasmin' is the strained and cooled decoction of 72; the drugs (kalka) are those listed in 72-76. 'prastha' is a unit of volume and is kept in Sanskrit. The item 'measured by a prastha' is given in 78.

words.gloss: born of the testes of boar, buffalo and he-goat

hindi: रस, सूअर, भैंसे और बकरे के मुष्कों यानी अण्डकोशों से उत्पन्न, उसी प्रकार।
english: The juice (rasa) arising from the testes of the boar, buffalo and he-goat, likewise.
notes: 'mahiṣa' = buffalo (a male is meant by context, not stated; the text says only 'mahiṣa'). Whether the three animals each give their own prastha or are taken together is not stated. The sentence is not complete here (continues after the unit).
